::: {#sol-one-seed}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
narrow_scores = torch.tensor([train_and_score(32, 0.1, seed)[-1] for seed in range(10)])
mean_gap = (wide_scores.mean() - narrow_scores.mean()).item()
gap_se = ((wide_scores.var() + narrow_scores.var()) / 10).sqrt().item()
print(narrow_scores.mean().item(), wide_scores.mean().item(), mean_gap, gap_se)
# Stop the render if the prose below stops being true.
assert abs(wide_seed0 - narrow_seed0) < seed_high - seed_low
assert abs(mean_gap) < 2 * gap_se
```

No.
The two runs differ by `r sprintf("%.3f", abs(py$wide_seed0 - py$narrow_seed0))`,
less than the `r sprintf("%.3f", py$seed_high - py$seed_low)` that the seed alone moved [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 64 in @sol-seed-spread.
With ten seeds of each,
the mean [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) of width 64 is higher by `r sprintf("%.4f", py$mean_gap)`.
That difference has [standard error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-standard-error) `r sprintf("%.4f", py$gap_se)`,
so it is less than two standard errors from 0,
and ten seeds each do not settle the question either.
A comparison of single runs measures the two seeds as much as the two [widths](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width).

:::
